title: BeyondTrust Privileged Sessions Started Outside Business Hours
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'BeyondTrust Privileged Sessions Started Outside Business Hours' only. Does not replace full SIEM correlation, IdP cloud-native analytics, or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `iam_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `iam_beyondtrust_privileged_sessions_started_outside_` (UC-9.4.24), SOC dashboard panel "IAM — BeyondTrust Privileged Sessions Started Outside Business Hours", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:iam_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=pam` sourcetype='beyondtrust:session' that satisfy the UC-9.4.24 SPL filters for 'BeyondTrust Privileged Sessions Started Outside Business Hours'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `pam` / `beyondtrust:session` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `iam_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-9.4.24.

dataSources: `sourcetype=beyondtrust:session` (or normalized PAM session events forwarded from BeyondTrust) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: BeyondTrust TA / Splunk CIM Email & Authentication patterns (org deployment) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=pam sourcetype="beyondtrust:session" earliest=-7d
| eval user=coalesce(user, UserName, admin_user, "")
| eval hour=strftime(_time, "%H")
| eval dow=strftime(_time, "%u")
| where (hour<7 OR hour>=19) OR dow IN ("6","7")
| stats count values(target_host) as targets by user
| sort -count
description: Privileged PAM sessions that begin late night or on weekends warrant review because they align with ransomware operators and rogue administrators evading oversight.
value: Operationalizes a simple time-based control that works even when session recordings are retained elsewhere, giving SOC analysts a prioritized review queue.
implementation: Adjust business-hour boundaries and weekend definition for your locale. Map `target_host` field names to your parser. Exclude maintenance accounts via lookup. Pair with on-call schedules to reduce false positives.
visualization: Table (user × targets), timeline of off-hours sessions, pie (weekday vs weekend).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable: this use case is not built on a CIM data model. Rely on the search in Step 2 against your raw directory, IdP, PAM, or device feeds.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled IAM maintenance** — Planned directory or IdP change generates expected deviations for 'BeyondTrust Privileged Sessions Started Outside Business Hours'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Onboarding burst** — New accounts or apps produce atypical `pam` volume.

3. **Monitoring synthetic bind checks** — Health probes from known scanner hosts.

4. **Stale application credential** — Single entity dominates `beyondtrust:session` failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `iam_exception_register.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure: BeyondTrust TA / Splunk CIM Email & Authentication patterns (org deployment).
• Data sources: `sourcetype=beyondtrust:session` (or normalized PAM session events forwarded from BeyondTrust).

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Adjust business-hour boundaries and weekend definition for your locale. Map `target_host` field names to your parser. Exclude maintenance accounts via lookup. Pair with on-call schedules to reduce false positives.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

```spl
index=pam sourcetype="beyondtrust:session" earliest=-7d
| eval user=coalesce(user, UserName, admin_user, "")
| eval hour=strftime(_time, "%H")
| eval dow=strftime(_time, "%u")
| where (hour<7 OR hour>=19) OR dow IN ("6","7")
| stats count values(target_host) as targets by user
| sort -count
```

Step 3 — Validate
Compare with BeyondTrust session history in the vendor console for the same users, targets, and timestamps.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add to a dashboard or alert; document the owner. Table (user × targets), timeline of off-hours sessions, pie (weekday vs weekend).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (BeyondTrust TA / Splunk CIM Email & Authentication patterns (org deployment) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=beyondtrust:session into pam. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`hour, user`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We flag when someone starts a privileged vault session at odd hours so you can review before off-hours access turns into unnoticed abuse.
